title: Projection formulas form a coefficient tower
statement:
Let $f:X\to Y$ be a morphism of schemes, with the ordinary unbounded pro-etale derived operations $Lf^*\dashv Rf_*$ of [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations], and let $K\in D(X_{\mathrm{proet}},\Lambda)$. Use the coefficient datum $(\Lambda,I)$ and $P_n=\Lambda/I^n$ for $n\geq1$ of [def-weil-pbc-complete-coefficient-datum]. Coefficient complexes are constant sheaves on the indicated site; on $X$ they are identified with their pullbacks from $Y$. All maps below are in $D(Y_{\mathrm{proet}},\Lambda)$, after restriction of scalars, not maps between different quotient-coefficient categories. Choose bounded finite-projective representatives of the perfect $\Lambda$-complexes $P_n$, and use the arrows $\pi_n,\rho_n$ of [def-weil-pbc-projection-formula-arrows] for these representatives. For every $n\geq1$, let $q_n:P_{n+1}\to P_n$ be the quotient. The square

$$
\begin{CD}
(Rf_*K)\otimes^LP_{n+1} @>{\pi_{n+1}}>>
Rf_*(K\otimes^LP_{n+1})\\
@V{1\otimes q_n}VV @VV{Rf_*(1\otimes q_n)}V\\
(Rf_*K)\otimes^LP_n @>{\pi_n}>> Rf_*(K\otimes^LP_n)
\end{CD}
$$

commutes, and so does the square with every $\pi$ replaced by $\rho$ and
horizontal arrows reversed; its vertical arrows remain the two quotient
maps.

proof.text: Write $L=Lf^*$ and $R=Rf_*$, and let $\epsilon:LR\to1$ be the counit. Put $L=Lf^*$ and $R=Rf_*$. The datum [def-weil-pbc-complete-coefficient-datum] supplies the perfect complexes $P_n$ and the quotient maps. Perfectness over the ring means precisely the existence of a bounded finite-projective representative [def-pc-perfect-ring-complex]; choose one for each $n$, with splittings as in [def-weil-pbc-strict-perfect-coefficient-package]. The operations [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations] supply an exact coefficient-preserving inverse image and the unbounded derived adjunction. To justify the constant-coefficient identifications, inverse image preserves constant sheaves: for a constant object with value $M$, its maps to a sheaf $H$ are maps from $M$ to global sections of $H$; adjunction and $(f_*H)(Y)=H(X)$ give the same description on either site. Thus the two objects represent the same functor, naturally in $M$. This applies to modules and their ring actions, hence to $P_n$ and $q_n$. Exactness allows this identification termwise in the derived category. No flatness of $P_n$ over $\Lambda$ is claimed.

source.place: Tag 07A6 (lemma-adjoint); coefficient convention and elementary constant-object adjunction calculation

proof.text: For a coefficient object $P$, let $t_P:L(RK\otimes^LP)\xrightarrow{\sim}LRK\otimes^LLP$ be the bifunctorial comparison of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback]. By [def-weil-pbc-projection-formula-arrows], the transpose of $\pi_P$ is $a_P=(\epsilon_K\otimes1_{LP})t_P$. Set $P=P_{n+1}$, $Q=P_n$, $q=q_n$, $u=1_{RK}\otimes q$ and $v=1_K\otimes Lq$. Under the adjunction [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations], the transpose of $R(v)\pi_P$ is $v a_P$: explicitly, $\epsilon_{K\otimes LQ}LR(v)L\pi_P=v\epsilon_{K\otimes LP}L\pi_P$ by counit naturality. The transpose of $\pi_Q u$ is $a_Q L(u)$ by functoriality of $L$.

Naturality of $t$ in its second variable [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback] gives $t_Q L(u)=(1_{LRK}\otimes Lq)t_P$. The interchange law for the tensor bifunctor gives $(\epsilon_K\otimes1_{LQ})(1_{LRK}\otimes Lq)=(1_K\otimes Lq)(\epsilon_K\otimes1_{LP})$. Consequently $a_Q L(u)=v a_P$. The bijection of the adjunction [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations] is injective, so the two original morphisms are equal: $R(v)\pi_{n+1}=\pi_n u$. Under step 1's constant-coefficient identifications, this is exactly the forward quotient square.

source.place: Tags 07A4 and 07A6; explicit tensor interchange and injectivity of the adjunction bijection

proof.text: Apply [lemma-weil-pbc-projection-formula-totalization] to the bounded finite-projective representatives chosen in step 1. It gives both $\rho_j\pi_j=1$ and $\pi_j\rho_j=1$, for $j=n,n+1$, for the constructed $\rho_j$ (not merely an unspecified inverse). Compose step 3's equality on the left with $\rho_n$ and on the right with $\rho_{n+1}$. Associativity and these identities give $\rho_n R(v)=u\rho_{n+1}$, which is the reversed-horizontal square with the same downward quotient maps. For a chosen identification $s:F^\bullet\xrightarrow{\sim}P_j$, the forward naturality calculation of steps 2–3, applied to $s$, gives $R(1_K\otimes Ls)\pi_F=\pi_{P_j}(1_{RK}\otimes s)$. Thus conjugating $\pi_F$ along these two isomorphisms gives the fixed arrow $\pi_{P_j}$. Conjugating its constructed inverse gives an inverse of that same arrow. Any two such inverses $b,c$ satisfy $b=b\pi_{P_j}c=c$, proving independence of both representatives and splittings.
